title: Vaulting and Break-Glass Field Guide: RBAC v2 + SIEM Evidence Exports
content:
Purpose:
This field guide is a compact, operational runbook for day-to-day secrets lifecycle and emergency access (break-glass) at Redwood Inference. It ties RBAC v2 role mappings to our vaulting patterns, defines the audit event schema we export to the SIEM, and documents the minimal evidence automation flow used during incidents.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: on-call SREs, infra engineers, security responders, and compliance reviewers.
- Scope: service account keys, API tokens, database credentials, KMS/HSM references, and ephemeral access tokens. Not a policy doc — this is the operational checklist and sample payloads for tool integrations.

Quick summary of changes from v1 runbooks:
- RBAC v2 role bindings replace team-wide vault policies; access is explicit per resource and time-limited by default.
- SIEM export schema standardized to reduce downstream parsing work (see Audit Log Schema section).
- Evidence automation pipeline implemented to capture snapshots on any break-glass event.

RBAC v2 role mappings (operational view):
- role:svc-db-rotator -> permissions: read/write to secret path secret/databases/*, create/rotate subkeys, no console login. Assigned to service owner only. TTL enforced: 24h.
- role:eng-oncall -> permissions: read-only to secret/metafiles/*, ability to create ephemeral tokens scoped to secret/*:readonly. Must use 2FA and require approval ticket for elevated roles.
- role:platform-admin -> permissions: full secret/*, but protected by jump policy (break-glass flow) and audited.

Credential inventory snapshot format (single line per secret; stored in inventory CSV elsewhere but we include canonical fields here):
- secret_id | logical_path | owner | env | last_rotated | rotation_method | criticality | notes
- example: sql-analytics-prod | secret/databases/analytics/prod | svc-analytics | prod | 2024-02-01 | lambda-rotation | P0 | uses read-replica creds

Rotation policy matrix (operational defaults):
- P0 service credentials (DB write keys, KMS signing): rotate every 30 days, automated via rotation-lambda, immediate rotation on suspect access.
- P1 service credentials (API keys for internal services): rotate every 90 days, can be manual if flagged.
- P2 long-lived integration keys (third-party) : rotate annually, exception workflow required.
- Human user API tokens: short-lived by default (12h ephemeral), personal tokens discouraged.

Vault access patterns and recommendations:
- Always prefer ephemeral tokens (Vault approle/oidc) with minimum scopes.
- Use named service principals rather than reusing engineering members’ tokens.
- Store KMS references in vault instead of storing plaintext keys in config repositories.
- For on-prem vault clusters, ensure mirrors to hosted logging endpoints to preserve evidence exports.

Break-Glass procedure (step-by-step):
1) Trigger: Pager or manual declaration of emergency with impact to availability or security.
2) Create incident ticket (Jira) tagged break_glass and assign security lead.
3) Request temporary elevation via the break-glass API endpoint. API enforces: requestor identity, reason, approver (on-call-sec), requested TTL (max 4 hours), justification note.
4) Approval: manual approval required by a designated approver unless global emergency mode is enabled (rare; requires exec-level sign-off).
5) On approval: system issues a time-limited token and records AUDIT event type=break_glass.grant with metadata (see Audit Log Schema). Evidence automation immediately snapshots environment: list of active sessions, last 100 access events on affected secret paths, process list for affected hosts, and a memory-resident scrubber run.
6) Post-incident: require forced rotation of any secrets that were accessed during break-glass, full forensic review within 72 hours, and retention of evidence bundle in secure escrow for 1 year.

Audit Log Schema (canonical fields we export to SIEM):
- event_id: UUIDv4
- timestamp: ISO-8601
- actor.principal: username or service principal (string)
- actor.type: human | service | system
- action: read | write | create | rotate | revoke | break_glass.request | break_glass.grant | token.create | token.revoke
- resource.path: vault logical path (e.g. secret/databases/analytics/prod)"
content_continued:
- resource.type: secret | kms_ref | cert | token
- result: success | failure | partial
- client.ip: IPv4/IPv6 or NAT info
- request.id: internal request correlation id
- request.duration_ms: numeric
- audit.reason: free text (optional)
- approver: username (for break_glass.grant)

Example event (single-line JSON example for SIEM ingestion):
{"event_id":"b1a3f8c4-6dfe-4d2b-9c71-e7f9b3e6a2f1","timestamp":"2024-03-01T14:12:02Z","actor.principal":"svc-deploy-bot","actor.type":"service","action":"token.create","resource.path":"auth/approle/role/deployer/login","resource.type":"token","result":"success","client.ip":"34.82.11.9","request.id":"req-9f8c","request.duration_ms":112}
content_final:
SIEM export mapping (fields -> destination indices):
- Splunk: index=redwood_audit, sourcetype=vault:audit, kv_mode=none, use _time from timestamp. We add event_id and request.id for dedupe.
- Chronicle: insert as JSON with event_id as traceId, map actor.principal to userName field.
- Datadog: submit as logs with attributes tags: team:<owner-team>, env:<prod/stage>.

Evidence automation flow (what runs automatically when a high-severity access happens or break-glass is granted):
- Trigger: detection rule in SIEM (suspicious token creation, wildcard path access, break_glass.grant) or manual run by responder.
- Collector actions (automated):
  - pull last 7 days of vault audit events for affected paths (JSON lines),
  - snapshot active tokens bound to the principal,
  - query orchestration to list recent deploys and code-owners for services referencing the secret path,
  - collect logs for 30 minutes before/after the event from host logging buckets,
  - store bundle in secure evidence bucket with write-once retention and HSM key seal.

Operational commands (examples) — treat these as pseudo-commands (ops automation implements wrappers):
- vault search "secret/databases/analytics/prod" --show-meta
- ops break-glass request --actor a.kapoor --reason "DB restore" --ttl 02:00 --ticket JIRA-4321
- ops evidence collect --path secret/databases/analytics/prod --since 2024-03-01T00:00Z
- gitlab-ci: rotate-secret --service sql-analytics-prod --method lambda

Post-incident requirements (minimum):
- rotate any secrets with confirmed or potential access during break-glass within 24h.
- deliver a short incident summary to security@redwood.com with list of rotated secret_ids and evidence bundle id.
- update credential inventory row with last_rotated and incident reference.

Operational gotchas and notes:
- Don’t use long-lived admin policies for daily ops — prefer ephemeral scopes.
- Some third-party integrations still require stored OAuth tokens. Tag these as P2 and track manual rotation ownership.
- Vault telemetry ingestion occasionally duplicates events when HA failover happens; SIEM ingestion dedupe keyed on event_id.

Open questions / action items (owner):
- Implement automatic crosscheck that flags secrets referenced in IaC repos but not present in the inventory (owner: Daniel Ortiz)
- Add stronger approval flow for break-glass when approver is the requestor (owner: Maya Chen)
- Consolidate SIEM parsers to a shared library (owner: Ethan Rivera)

Appendix A — Minimal evidence checklist for compliance auditors:
- Incident ticket id and timeline (Jira link)
- Audit export file (JSON lines) for affected secret paths
- Snapshots of issued tokens and session list at time of break-glass grant
- Rotation action logs and confirmation (who rotated what and when)
- Signed attestation from approving manager

Appendix B — Contacts and escalation list (on-call rotation):
- Security lead: Maya Chen (pager)
- SRE on-call: Daniel Ortiz (pager)
- Platform lead: Ethan Rivera (email)
notes: Draft operational runbook designed to be concise and executed by responders. This doc intentionally mixes sample command references and checklist items; formal procedures live in Confluence linked artifacts.
